chapter: Youth, Storyville and the bands he heard
title: Carnival clubs, addresses he lived at, and his 1914 marriage
summary: He never played carnival parades; lists where he lived; married in 1914 when just starting trumpet.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What about some of these clubs? Did you ever play for the, down in Araby, for the carnival club?
No, no, no. I know they had the parades. Yeah, I never prayed for either one of them.

You never marched at carnival parades, huh? No, no. Do you remember some of the different, uh, addresses where you lived there? Oh, that's kind of hard. Yeah, sometimes that helps you remember which band you were with, you know? Yeah, yeah. You could say I lived at Durban Inn, Romana.

Yeah, well, uh, let's see, you know, before I was married, I lived at 5327 Dolphin Street. And I'm married, I lived at, uh, 822 Hyde Street, I think it was. And I moved from there, I moved, what we call uptown, Washington and Durban Inn, Durban Inn. Then from there, I moved to Durban Inn, between 2nd and 3rd. From there, I moved to Desire and Tondi. Mm. From there, I moved on Havana and, uh, near Law. And I don't know now, from there where I went.
Well, we're at St. Bernard Avenue now, huh? Yeah. What's the number, 1413?
What instrument were you playing when you got married?
Just starting food with that trumpet. Oh, yeah.
Did you play at your wedding reception?
Don Elbert did that. You don't remember Don Elbert?
Yeah, he lived over there on Robinson Street. I remember him, but I don't know about him playing for his...

I guess he did. Well, I'll tell you what, me at that time, I wasn't good enough. Maybe I might have done the same thing, but I couldn't play instrument good enough. You got started. Yeah, you got started.
